Past editions have focused on specific Central American countries (El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua); the programme runs in successive regional editions.

amount.note: Up to USD 2,100 per fellow; 10 fellowships awarded per edition.

grants.notes: Runs as successive regional editions (e.g. 'Triángulo Norte y Nicaragua'); exact current-edition deadline could not be confirmed, so left null. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Fundación Gabo's flagship annual scholarship programme funds journalism projects by journalists across Latin America, with 25 scholarships ranging from USD 2,500 to USD 8,000 awarded per cycle.

amount.note: 25 scholarships awarded per cycle, amounts ranging between the stated min and max.

grants.notes: One source described this cycle's application window as closing around 1 July, which (if referring to 2026) has already passed; the exact year could not be confirmed on the funder's own page, so the deadline field is left null. Open to journalists from any Latin American country. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Grants co-run with partner foundations (e.g. Fundación Avina, Habitat for Humanity) supporting investigative journalism on sustainable-development themes in Latin America, such as inclusive recycling. Winners receive a cash stipend plus access to editorial mentorship.

amount.note: USD 800 stipend cited for the 'Edición Hábitat' round; amount varies by themed edition.

grants.notes: Runs as a series of themed editions with different co-funders and topics (recycling, habitat, etc.); no current-edition deadline was confirmed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Judith Neilson Institute for Journalism and Ideas
grants.summary: JNI's general grants programme funds journalists and media organisations to produce public-interest journalism, with a particular focus on Australian reporting and on Asia. Freelancers are advised to apply with the backing of a media platform.

amount.note: Amount not stated.

grants.notes: News coverage from 2026 indicates JNI adopted a revised strategy under which it will no longer award grants to major news organisations, following organisational turbulence; scope and current status of smaller/individual grants could not be confirmed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Judith Neilson Institute for Journalism and Ideas (with the Walkley Foundation)
grants.summary: A grant administered with the Walkley Foundation to help Australian and permanent-resident freelance journalists produce a significant body of work, in any medium, reporting on Asia.

amount.note: Up to $25,000 cited; currency not explicitly stated in the source (the programme is Australian-run).

grants.notes: Restricted to Australian citizens/permanent residents. No 2026 application round could be confirmed; the most recent detailed information found dated to 2020, and JNI's 2026 strategy shift (see JNI Grants entry) may affect this programme's status. Marked closed pending confirmation of an active round. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A prototyping micro-grant fund helping news and media entrepreneurs in Asia ideate, launch, test and iterate news products and services. Splice does not take an equity stake in the ventures it supports.

amount.note: Described as micro-grants / pre-seed, non-equity funding; specific amount not stated.

grants.notes: For media startups/entrepreneurs building new news products, rather than individual freelance journalists. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: The sixth yearly Creative Europe cross-sectoral call funding transnational consortia of news media organisations on cross-border collaboration, sustainable business models and journalistic projects, including strand topics for economic resilience ('Collaborations') and support for media of particular democratic relevance such as local, community and investigative outlets ('Pluralism').

amount.note: Total call budget €13,800,000; maximum grant per project €2,000,000; co-financing rate up to 80% of eligible costs.

grants.notes: Requires a consortium of at least 3 independent entities from 3 different eligible countries; projects run 24 months, expected to start late 2026. Eligible countries include EU member states, EEA/associated countries, plus Georgia and Ukraine. This 2026 round's deadline (4 Feb 2026) has passed; it is an annually recurring call. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A Creative Europe cross-sectoral call funding innovative, cross-border media-literacy projects, open to consortia including media organisations, educational institutions and other bodies working to build public resilience against disinformation.

amount.note: Total indicative budget €3,000,000 for 2026; maximum grant per project €500,000; co-financing rate up to 70% of eligible costs.

grants.notes: Requires a consortium of at least 3 entities from 3 different Creative Europe-participating countries; projects run up to 2 years. Also open to Georgia and Ukraine. This round's deadline (11 March 2026) has passed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Nieman Foundation for Journalism, Harvard University
grants.summary: A fully funded academic-year fellowship for non-U.S. working journalists (including those working in the U.S.) to study at Harvard University, audit classes, and take part in Nieman seminars and events. Fellows receive a living stipend plus child care and health insurance allowances and must refrain from professional work during the fellowship year.

amount.note: $87,500 stipend paid over a nine-month period to cover living costs; additional child care allowance (up to $16,750/year for 4+ children) and health insurance supplement (up to $6,250) also available, per the funder's Stipend & Allowances page.

grants.notes: Recurring annual deadline of December 1 stated on the funder's page for the International Nieman Fellowship (exact year not stated verbatim, so left as recurring rather than a fixed date). Nine-month academic-year fellowship, fellow relocates to Cambridge, MA. Requires 5+ years of full-time media experience (freelancers explicitly eligible); no PR/corporate-comms work; must speak/read/write English fluently; must not have done a residential fellowship of 4+ months in the prior 5 years. Must reside in Cambridge, MA during the fellowship and refrain from paid professional work except as approved. A designated Nieman-Berkman Klein Fellowship in Journalism Innovation track exists within the same application. Visa note: applicants from countries where the U.S. has suspended nonimmigrant (J) visas are advised to wait unless they hold another eligible citizenship.

grants.funder: Nieman Foundation for Journalism, Harvard University
grants.summary: A fully funded academic-year fellowship for U.S.-citizen working journalists (including those working outside the U.S.) to study at Harvard University, audit classes, and take part in Nieman seminars and events. Fellows receive a living stipend plus child care and health insurance allowances and must refrain from professional work during the fellowship year.

amount.note: $87,500 stipend paid over a nine-month period to cover living costs; additional child care allowance (up to $16,750/year for 4+ children) and health insurance supplement (up to $6,250) also available, per the funder's Stipend & Allowances page.

grants.notes: Recurring annual deadline of January 31 stated on the funder's page for the U.S. Nieman Fellowship (exact year not stated verbatim, so left as recurring rather than a fixed date). Nine-month academic-year fellowship, fellow relocates to Cambridge, MA. Same eligibility rules as the international track: 5+ years full-time media experience, freelancers explicitly eligible, no PR/corporate-comms work, English fluency required.

grants.funder: John S. Knight Journalism Fellowships, Stanford University
grants.summary: A nine-month residential fellowship at Stanford University for up to 20 journalists per year from around the world to work collaboratively on journalism's most urgent challenges, with personalized mentorship and access to Stanford classes. The 2026-27 class received a stipend of $130,000 plus Stanford health insurance for fellows, spouses, and children, and included both newsroom staff, freelancers, and people supporting journalism organisations.

amount.note: $130,000 stipend and Stanford health insurance for fellows, spouses and children, as stated for the 2026-27 (Class of 2027) cohort; figure not explicitly guaranteed to repeat for future cycles on the fetched page.

grants.notes: Nine-month residential fellowship in Stanford, California; fellow relocates for the term. The fetched homepage and news pages did not state an application deadline or opening date for the next cycle; see the funder's Application FAQ page for current dates. Up to 20 fellows/year; the 2026-27 class (13 fellows) included 8 U.S. and 5 international fellows, drawn from news organisations, freelancers, and organisations supporting journalists. Fellows have a personal coach (director) throughout the year; partners ('affiliates') are welcome at most gatherings.

grants.funder: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford
grants.summary: A programme for practising, mid-career journalists and editors to spend three or six months in Oxford researching a personal project, with most fellows fully funded (fees, monthly stipend, travel and visa costs covered). Fellowships begin in October, January or April and require a minimum of five years' journalistic experience; freelancers may apply but those in PR/corporate communications may not.

amount.note: Most fellows are fully funded: fees covered plus a monthly stipend of £2,000 to cover accommodation, food and general living expenses, with travel to/from the UK and visa costs also covered. Some fellows instead come via sponsoring organisations with their own funding and selection process (e.g. Thomson Reuters Foundation Fellowship, Mona Megalli Fellowship for a Middle East journalist).

grants.notes: As of the fetched pages (18 Sep 2026), applications for fellowships beginning in the 2026-27 academic year are stated as closed on two separate fetched pages, with the programme reopening in January 2027 for cohorts starting October 2026, January 2027 or April 2027; exact reopening date not stated. One page fragment inconsistently also read 'applications are now open' — likely stale cached content — so this was not relied on for status. Fellowship lasts three or six months in Oxford, UK; fellow relocates for the term. Requires 5+ years' journalistic experience; open to journalists worldwide; not open to PR/public affairs/corporate communications staff; fellows must plan to return to journalism afterward.

grants.funder: Wallace House Center for Journalists, University of Michigan
grants.summary: An eight-month residential fellowship (late August through April) at the University of Michigan for journalists with at least five years of experience, including freelancers, to pursue a self-directed course of study. The programme includes a living stipend, relocation allowance, health insurance, and University of Michigan course auditing, with typically up to six international fellows joining ten to twelve U.S. journalists each year.

amount.note: Reported as an $85,000 stipend disbursed monthly August through April, plus a $5,000 relocation allowance and health insurance coverage. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.notes: No snapshot available for this source; sourced via WebSearch of secondary pages referencing wallacehouse.umich.edu content, not the funder's own page directly. Eight-month residential fellowship, Ann Arbor, Michigan; fellow relocates for the term. International applications for the 2026-27 cohort are described as closed, with applications for 2027-28 said to open in October 2026 (exact date not given). Up to six international fellows typically join ten to twelve U.S. journalists; international finalists are interviewed in January/February to allow time for visa processing. Requires 5+ years of journalism experience. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A three-month fellowship at the IWM in Vienna giving European journalists time off from their regular duties to pursue in-depth, independent research on a topic of their choice. Fellows receive a monthly stipend plus office space and access to the IWM academic community.

amount.note: Monthly stipend for the 3-month term.

grants.notes: Term runs three consecutive months, placement at the IWM in Vienna, between September 2026 and June 2027 for the cohort tied to this deadline. Open to European journalists (including Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Turkey) with several years' professional experience in print, broadcast or online journalism; no explicit language requirement stated. The 16 January 2026 deadline for this cycle has passed; the call recurs annually but the next deadline is not yet confirmed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Grants and Investments — Storytelling grants (Explorer Level I/II)
grants.summary: National Geographic Society's Explorer grants fund project leaders in conservation, education, research, storytelling and technology; the storytelling category explicitly covers journalism, photography, filmmaking and digital media. The Society has moved to a request-for-proposals model with themed windows rather than a standing rolling call.

amount.note: Level I grants up to $20,000; Level II grants up to $100,000 for established applicants pushing for significant impact.

grants.notes: Applicants must be 18+; those working outside their home country must include a local collaborator. The Society's own page currently lists no open opportunities and states a storytelling-related application window opens 1 October 2026; specific deadline and amount for that window were not stated in available evidence. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: National Geographic Society (with The Climate Pledge)
grants.programme: National Geographic Society × The Climate Pledge Storytelling Grant
grants.summary: A partnership between the National Geographic Society and The Climate Pledge funding storytelling projects on climate resilience, energy transition and sustainability solutions. Open to professional storytellers, journalists, documentary filmmakers, photographers, writers and podcast producers worldwide, whether or not they have previously held National Geographic Explorer status.

amount.note: Up to $100,000; early-career applicants (5 years or less experience) advised to request no more than $20,000. Project implementation period up to 2 years.

grants.notes: 2026 cycle deadline was 25 May 2026, 11:59pm EDT; applications submitted in English via NatGeo's online portal. Covers climate & energy transition, nature & land systems, and human & built systems topics. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Heinrich Böll Stiftung (Washington, DC / North America Office)
grants.summary: Supports journalists based in the US, Canada or Germany (and, for Global South-focused stories, journalists in Africa, Asia and Latin America) to research and report transatlantic stories on climate & energy, democracy, foreign & security, technology, or global development policy. Fellows choose either an on-the-ground track including travel or a remote/digital track.

amount.note: Reported as $2,000 for the digital/remote track (no travel) and $4,000 for the on-the-ground track (with travel); figures not verified on the funder's own page.

grants.notes: Run out of the Heinrich Böll Stiftung's Washington, DC office rather than the German headquarters site. Secondary sources give conflicting application-deadline dates (13 March vs 24 March) and fellows are expected to submit a first draft by 1 October and publish by year-end, meaning the 2026 cohort's window has already closed as of this check. Exact current-cycle deadline and amount could not be confirmed on the funder's own page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung — Media Programme South East Europe
grants.summary: A scholarship for Bachelor's students (from their 2nd academic year) and Master's students of any major who are already actively engaged at a media outlet, at universities across South-East Europe. Scholars receive a monthly grant and access to exchanges with regional and international media experts.

amount.note: Monthly grant amount not stated in the pages reviewed.

grants.notes: Applicants must show a distinctive interest in social/political issues and alignment with KAS's values (democracy, freedom, rule of law, pluralism, European unification). Universities in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Romania and Serbia are covered. Most recently reported call closed 10 June 2025; recurs each academic year/semester but the 2026 deadline could not be confirmed on the funder's own page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Adenauer Fellowship for Media and Communication
grants.summary: Supports young journalists from Bangladesh, India, Pakistan and the Philippines (with related country-specific tracks also open to journalists in Indonesia and Malaysia) to pursue a Master's degree in journalism, combining a semester grant, tuition support and study-related travel costs.

amount.note: Semester grant of EUR 500 plus tuition fees up to EUR 6,000, plus study-related travel costs.

grants.notes: Applicants must be 35 or under at the start of postgraduate study, have at least 2 years' relevant work experience, and be fluent in English at C1 level or above. Details were assembled from multiple secondary scholarship-database listings that may conflate slightly different regional tracks; a related 2026 call for Indonesia/Malaysia journalists had a stated deadline of 31 March 2026, already passed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Brings two journalists a year from countries with restricted press and information freedoms to Berlin for a six-month stay focused on rest, protection and recovery, for example after reporting from conflict zones or under state-security pressure. Run annually since 2015, and since 2026 organised independently by the taz Panter Stiftung in cooperation with Reporters Without Borders.

amount.note: Travel costs reimbursed, Berlin accommodation organised, pocket money provided, and free local public transport for up to 3 months; no stipend figure stated.

grants.notes: Six-month Berlin stay (reported as May–October 2026 for this cohort) for two journalists worldwide from countries with restricted press/information freedoms; no language or minimum-experience requirement stated. This cohort's application window (15 Dec 2025 – 15 Jan 2026) has closed; recurs annually. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Sends around ten journalists working in Germany on a group study trip to Washington D.C., Philadelphia and New York to examine the US media landscape, followed by a period of independent research. Applicants submit a CV and a short English-language motivation letter describing their research project.

amount.note: Covers travel, accommodation and programme costs for the 12-day group trip, and partially covers costs for the following 9-day period of independent research.

grants.notes: Open to journalists working in Germany with sufficient English; age and nationality are not restricted. 2026 trip runs September/October 2026; the informal-application deadline (8 March 2026) has passed. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Funds two 18-month traineeships per year in the taz newsroom for aspiring journalists with diverse backgrounds who lack classical journalism training or credentials, explicitly welcoming applicants who face discrimination based on origin, religion, gender, gender identity or disability.

amount.note: Each traineeship reportedly costs the foundation approximately EUR 25,000 (donation-funded); this funds the placement rather than being a grant paid directly to the applicant.

grants.notes: 18-month in-house traineeship at taz rotating through newsroom departments; no formal degree or certificate required. 2026 intake (deadline 18 Feb 2026, start June 2026) has already begun; recurs annually. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A 12-month programme supporting 15-20 African storytellers — including journalists, content creators, podcasters, vloggers and data visualizers — to produce original, research-informed content connecting climate change with debt, gender inequality and fossil fuel extraction across ten African countries. Selected storytellers receive training, mentorship, content amplification and a grant.
grants.eligibleActivity: Africa No Filter's mission is shifting narratives about Africa rather than funding journalism specifically, but this call explicitly lists journalists among its eligible applicant types alongside other content creators, and requires the funded output to be original, research-informed content on climate justice; a journalist may apply provided the resulting published work and its rights remain their own, which is the programme's stated individual-applicant condition.

amount.note: Grant of up to US$4,000 per storyteller, plus training, mentorship and content amplification, over a 12-month programme.

grants.notes: Deadline (25 Sep 2026, 6pm GMT) and amount confirmed both in today's GFMD listing and via secondary reposts citing Africa No Filter's own site. Only individual applicants (no organisations/agencies) may apply. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Call for Project Proposals: Promotion of Human Rights in Ukraine 2027
grants.summary: The German Embassy in Kyiv funds human-rights projects in Ukraine for 2027 under three priority areas: countering disinformation (including support for press/media freedom and securing evidence for accountability and justice, with a focus on defending against SLAPP suits), promoting children's rights, and addressing gender-based violence. Eligibility is limited to Ukrainian media organisations, and the process begins with a short project concept.

amount.note: GFMD lists 'EUR 50,000 - 150,00' (likely a typo for 150,000); exact ceiling not independently confirmed.

grants.notes: Two-stage process: a short project concept due 27 Sep 2026; only shortlisted applicants invited to submit a full application. Project must be completed by end of 2027. Eligibility restricted to Ukrainian media organisations per GFMD. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Professional Development Grants for Environmental Journalism (Earth Services)
grants.summary: A capacity-building grant, funded by Arcadia, for organisations to deliver collective development and support services — such as training sessions, coaching or fellowship programmes — that build the skills of professional environmental investigative journalists in Europe. Individuals cannot apply; only incorporated legal entities with a track record working with journalists and/or on environmental issues are eligible.

amount.note: Around €75,000 available per call, to be distributed among supported projects.

grants.notes: Referenced (in truncated form) on today's Journalismfund Europe snapshot; deadline schedule (22 Jan, 23 Apr, 20 Aug 2026) and funder (Arcadia) confirmed via web search of the funder's own grants portal. This 2026 cycle's deadlines have all passed; no 2027 dates announced yet. Not confirmed in full on the captured snapshot text.

grants.summary: Annual $5,000 grants to women or nonbinary journalists reporting on subculture and unconventional narrative topics, honoring journalist Kim Wall who was killed while on assignment in 2017.

amount.note: Single grant tier of $5,000.

grants.notes: New entry, previously untracked; found via today's IWMF site nav but the detail page was not among today's captured snapshot pages, so verified via web search instead. Open worldwide to women/nonbinary journalists with 1+ years' professional experience and strong English skills; internships don't count toward experience. Most recent (2026) cycle deadline was 7 Dec 2025; grantees announced March 2026. Next cycle timing not yet announced. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Fellowship of up to $2,000 for U.S.-based women and nonbinary journalists from underrepresented backgrounds, supporting a reporting project or a professional development opportunity, created in memory of Quartz editor Lauren Brown.
grants.notes: New entry, previously untracked; found via today's IWMF site nav but the detail page was not among today's captured snapshot pages, so verified via web search instead. U.S.-based women/nonbinary journalists from underrepresented backgrounds; funds either a reporting project or a professional-development/skills opportunity. Most recent known cycle deadline was 20 July 2025; no 2026 cycle deadline found. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Emergency assistance for U.S.-based journalists of any gender who have been targeted, harmed or put at risk as a result of their reporting on politically charged events such as elections and civil unrest. Covers both immediate needs (medical aid, replacing stolen/destroyed equipment, protective gear) and longer-term needs (trauma and mental health support, legal referrals).

amount.note: Per-applicant amount not stated.

grants.notes: New entry, previously untracked; supported by the Ford Foundation and Press Forward; open to staff and independent (freelance) journalists; applications reviewed on an ongoing rolling basis, in order received; must show proof of financial need. This page was not among today's captured snapshot pages, so verified via web search instead. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.programme: Story Grants: Mining, Environment and Human Rights Reporting in Africa
grants.summary: Story grants of US$2,000 paired with a virtual media workshop, for journalists and social media content creators in Ghana, Uganda, DR Congo and South Africa to produce in-depth reporting on mining, environmental degradation and human rights.

amount.note: 10 story grants of US$2,000 each.

grants.notes: New entry, previously untracked. No snapshot available today (source fetch failed, HTTP 403); found via web search referencing the funder's own opportunities page, not read directly. Deadline of 6 September 2026 has passed; associated workshop runs 3-5 Nov 2026; story production/publication window is January-31 July 2027. Applications accepted in English or French. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: Travel scholarships for journalists who already received a Journalismfund Europe grant (European Cross-Border Grant or Earth Investigations Grant) and have been invited to present their published investigation at a conference, training or other public event. Covers registration, hotel and travel costs, refunded after the event against proof of expenses.

amount.note: Up to €1,250 for Earth Investigations Grant recipients, or up to €1,000 for European Cross-Border Grant recipients; food and drink not included. One scholarship per team per event.

grants.notes: This is NOT a standalone project grant: eligibility is restricted to journalists who already hold (or held) a Journalismfund Europe European Cross-Border Grant or Earth Investigations Grant, have published the resulting investigation, and have been invited to present it at an event. Reviewed on a rolling basis; decision within about two weeks. Reconfirmed verbatim on today's snapshot. No separate application portal - applicants email scholarships@journalismfund.eu directly.

grants.programme: MOVE Grants — Individual Mobility Across the Western Balkans
grants.summary: MOVE Grants provide short-term individual mobility funding for artists, cultural professionals, scholars, journalists, youth workers, CSO activists and other changemakers to travel to a host institution in another Western Balkans Contracting Party for a structured cooperation activity. A formal invitation letter from the host institution is required before anything else is assessed. Call 7 is currently open with a fixed October 2026 deadline.
grants.eligibleActivity: Journalists are explicitly named among the eligible individual applicant categories (alongside artists, scholars, youth workers and CSO activists) for this people-to-people mobility grant; a journalist could apply to travel to a host media organisation or institution in another WB6 country for a structured professional exchange or reporting-related activity.

amount.note: Up to 100% of eligible costs. Detailed cost-category caps are in the 15-page Guidelines for Applicants PDF, not fully captured here.

grants.notes: Individuals only, one application per call. Requires a formal partnership/invitation from a host institution in another WB6 Contracting Party (Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia); activities normally take place in the region. Implementation window Dec 2026-Apr 2027, final report due 30 April 2027. Other WBF schemes (GGI, GEFund, ERC, Matching Grants, WB6-V4 Fellowship) were checked but have no stated media/journalism eligibility route, so were not recorded.

grants.funder: European Centre for Press and Media Freedom (ECPMF)
grants.summary: The JiR Programme offers a relocation fellowship in Leipzig, Germany for journalists and media workers facing harassment and intimidation as a direct result of their work, providing a monthly stipend for a three- to six-month stay. A related JiR Kosovo strand, aimed at Ukrainian journalists, is currently not accepting new applications.

amount.note: Monthly stipend of €1,000 for the duration of the residency (3-6 months).

grants.notes: Eligible: journalists/media workers from EU Member States, Candidate Countries and Council of Europe Member States facing harassment or intimidation as a direct result of their work. Apply via a completed JiR Application Form / network-partner referral. The JiR Kosovo Programme (extra relocation and rent support, targeted at Ukrainian journalists) does not accept new applications at the moment.

grants.funder: European Centre for Press and Media Freedom (ECPMF)
grants.summary: ECPMF's Journalists-in-Exile Programme provides structured, ongoing support for media workers exiled in Germany, irrespective of country of origin. Support is in-kind: professional training, language courses, legal advice, help with recognition of qualifications, psychosocial support and procurement of journalistic equipment, rather than a cash grant.

amount.note: In-kind support only; ECPMF states it 'underlies strict funding criteria and is tied to limited project funds' and cannot support all incoming requests (this line is on ECPMF's own page).

grants.notes: For media workers currently exiled in Germany, regardless of origin. To apply, email support@ecpmf.eu describing your situation and you'll receive a questionnaire (English or German). Most eligibility/support detail here came from search results describing ECPMF's own pages rather than from today's snapshot capture. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: European Centre for Press and Media Freedom (ECPMF)
grants.summary: ECPMF offers free legal support and guidance to journalists and media outlets in Europe facing legal threats connected to their work. Applications are reviewed case-by-case by ECPMF's Legal Affairs Committee, which gives non-binding advice; the final decision on support rests with the ECPMF office.

amount.note: In-kind legal advice/guidance; no funding amount stated.

grants.notes: Apply by consulting ECPMF's guidelines, filling in the legal-support request template and emailing it in. Reviewed by the Legal Affairs Committee (LAC); final decision lies with the ECPMF office.

grants.funder: European Centre for Press and Media Freedom (ECPMF)
grants.programme: SAFE Project — Media Capacity Support Fund
grants.summary: Through the SAFE project, ECPMF offers training grants of up to €5,000 to independent media outlets in the Eastern Partnership region, funding training in journalist safety, digital security and media resilience so outlets can keep reporting safely under high-risk conditions.

amount.note: Training grants of up to €5,000 per programme.

grants.notes: Aimed at independent media outlets in Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine whose editorial teams pursue a public-interest mission and have limited access to other support. Secondary aggregators (fundsforNGOs, GFMD) report a 30 September 2026 deadline for the current call, but ECPMF's own page as captured today does not state a deadline, so it is left null/unknown here. Not confirmed on the funder's own page for the deadline specifically.

grants.funder: European Centre for Press and Media Freedom (ECPMF)
grants.programme: SAFE Project — Emergency and Psychological Support Funds
grants.summary: ECPMF's SAFE project plans an emergency support fund (for crises such as loss of professional equipment, medical emergencies or direct safety threats) and a psychological support fund (covering mental-health care from a provider of the journalist's choosing) for journalists and media workers in the Eastern Partnership. Both funds are listed on ECPMF's site as 'not open yet'.
grants.notes: Both funds are explicitly marked 'not open yet' on ECPMF's SAFE project page as captured today; no opening date is given. Worth re-checking in future sweeps.

grants.funder: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic
grants.programme: Transition Promotion Programme (TRANS) — Local Transition Projects
grants.summary: TRANS is the Czech MFA's framework for supporting human rights, democracy and civil-society development abroad. Local Transition Projects (LTPs) are run individually by Czech embassies and can fund work on rule of law, civic participation, and freedom of expression and information — including freedom of the media — implemented by non-governmental organisations.
grants.eligibleActivity: TRANS's own stated thematic pillars include 'promoting the freedom of expression and information, including the freedom of the media', alongside civil-society support, political participation and rule-of-law themes with no media component — so a newsroom or media NGO could apply for an LTP under that specific pillar, but the programme is not media-exclusive.

amount.note: A CZK 500,000 per-project ceiling for the most recently reported cycle comes from secondary/embassy sources, not from the MFA's own page as captured.

grants.notes: The programme is decentralised: each Czech embassy runs its own LTP call with its own budget, exact themes and deadline. The MFA's own page (captured today, only 268 words) just points to 'an overview of current grant calls' rather than listing terms itself. Reported cycle details (CZK 500,000 ceiling, 8 Dec 2025 deadline for a Mar-Oct 2026 project window, NGO-only implementer, four thematic pillars including media freedom) come from secondary aggregators and individual embassy call pages, not the MFA page captured today; that round's deadline has already passed and no newer cycle is visible on the captured page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A Dutch government fund supporting civil-society human rights work worldwide, disbursed mainly through periodic country-specific calls run by individual Dutch embassies. Interested applicants should check their nearest Dutch embassy's page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.
